name: Hair Transplant from 1000 up to 2000 Grafts
hướng dẫn sau dịch vụ:
"Hair Transplant Post-Operative Instructions
The First Night
The first night after your hair transplant is extremely important. Avoid touching the newly transplanted area under any circumstances.
You may experience mild itching, tenderness, or discomfort, which is completely normal. However, it is essential that you do not scratch or touch the transplanted grafts. Excessive touching may damage the hair follicles, reduce graft survival, and negatively affect the final results.
You may resume your normal daily activities one day after the procedure, provided that you follow your post-operative care instructions."
"Wearing a Hat
You may start wearing a loose-fitting hat 7 days after your procedure.
Please avoid wearing a hat indoors, as prolonged hat use may reduce airflow around the scalp and slow the healing process.
If you need to wear a hat for an extended period, choose one that is breathable and has ventilation holes to allow proper air circulation.
For the first 2 months, protect your scalp from direct sunlight. If you must stay outdoors under strong sunlight, cover your head with a loose hat."
"Sleeping Position
For the first 12 nights, sleep on your back with your head elevated.
We recommend using a travel neck pillow or placing a rolled towel under your neck to help maintain the correct sleeping position.
To prevent turning onto your side during sleep, place two large pillows alongside your shoulders to keep your body stable.
From the 8th day onward, you may begin sleeping slightly on your side, but continue to be careful not to place pressure on the transplanted area."
"Clothing
During the first week, wear clothing that opens from the front, such as shirts or zip-up jackets.
Avoid sweaters, turtlenecks, hoodies, or any garments that need to be pulled over your head.
If wearing such clothing is unavoidable, remove it very carefully. If possible, ask someone to assist you to prevent the fabric from rubbing against the transplanted area."
"Exercise and Physical Activities
Avoid all strenuous physical activities and sports for 1 month following your procedure.
After 2 weeks, you may begin light activities such as walking. We recommend taking a shower after exercising.
Avoid heavy workouts, weightlifting, or activities that may cause excessive sweating.
For 1 month, do not:
• Swim in the sea or a swimming pool
• Use a sauna or steam room
• Sunbathe
• Use a tanning bed (solarium)
Sexual activity should also be avoided during the first 5 days after surgery."
"Medications
To minimize swelling, prevent infection, and relieve discomfort, please take all medications prescribed by your doctor exactly as instructed.
Do not take any additional medications without consulting your physician. Certain medications may interfere with the healing process and could affect the success of your hair transplant, potentially voiding the treatment guarantee.
Unless your doctor advises otherwise, begin taking your medications on the evening after your procedure and continue until all prescribed tablets have been completed."
"Prescribed Medications
Ciprofloxacin (Cirprobay ) 500 mg (Antibiotic)
• Take 1 tablet twice daily (morning and evening).
• Take after meals.
Paracetamol (Hapacol không codein) (Pain Reliever)
• Take 1 tablet if needed for pain.
• Take after meals.
Methylprednisolone 16mg (Medrol) (Anti-inflammatory / Anti-swelling Medication)
• Take 3 tablets daily for the first 2 days.
• Then take 2 tablets daily until the medication is finished.
• The full course should be completed within 4 days.
• Take after meals.
Aspirin 100mg (Blood Thinner)
• Take 1 tablet once daily after meals."
"Bleeding
A small amount of bleeding after the procedure is completely normal.
If minor bleeding occurs, there is usually no cause for concern."
"Swelling
During the first 5 days, swelling and bruising around the forehead and face may occur due to the local anesthetic solution used during the procedure.
To help minimize swelling:
• Keep your head elevated whenever possible.
• Sit with your head upright.
• Rest on your back.
• Avoid blowing your nose forcefully.
• Avoid violent sneezing whenever possible.
Any swelling or bruising around the hairline should gradually subside within a few days.
Itching and Redness After Hair Transplant
Your scalp may appear pink or slightly red and may feel tight after the procedure. Mild itching is also a normal part of the healing process.
In some patients, the donor area may remain pink or slightly red for several weeks or even a few months. This is a normal part of the recovery process and will gradually improve over time.
Please avoid scratching or rubbing your scalp, even if itching occurs, as this may damage the newly transplanted grafts."
"Pimples After Hair Transplant
Small pimples may occasionally develop in both the transplanted area and the donor area during the healing process.
In many cases, these pimples are a normal sign that new hairs are beginning to grow through the skin.
However, in some cases, pimples may also indicate an infection that requires medical treatment.
If you notice pimples, redness, swelling, or any unusual changes on your scalp, please take clear photographs of the affected area and contact our medical team for further evaluation."
"Hair Care and Hair Washing Instructions
You may usually begin washing your hair 48 hours (2 days) after your hair transplant procedure unless your doctor advises otherwise.
Step 1
Apply the foam spray provided by our clinic to both the transplanted area and the donor area, taking care to avoid contact with your eyes.
Step 2
After approximately 30 seconds, the spray will begin to foam.
Leave the foam on your scalp for 30 minutes.
Step 3
Rinse your scalp gently using lukewarm water with low water pressure.
Do not touch, rub, or massage the transplanted area while rinsing.
You may gently wash the donor area.
Continue rinsing until all foam has been completely removed."
"Step 4
After washing, gently pat your hair dry using a paper towel.
Do not rub your scalp.
Do not use a hair dryer.
Please avoid using any hair spray, styling products, gels, waxes, or other cosmetic lotions on your scalp unless recommended by your doctor.
If You Have Any Concerns
If you notice anything unusual during your recovery or have any concerns about your scalp, please send us clear photographs and contact our medical team immediately.
We will be happy to evaluate your healing progress and provide further guidance if necessary."
"Hair Growth After Hair Transplant
Between 2 and 6 weeks after your hair transplant, the transplanted hairs may begin to fall out.
This process is known as shock loss (shock shedding) and is a completely normal stage of recovery.
Although the transplanted hairs fall out, the hair follicles remain healthy beneath the skin and will begin producing new hair.
New hair growth generally starts around the 4th month after the procedure.
The transplanted hair gradually becomes thicker and denser over the following months.
Final results are typically achieved between 8 and 12 months after surgery.
Please remember that every patient heals differently, and the speed and density of hair growth vary from person to person."
